Since we are given only the curve $r(t)$, we will use the cross product formula to find the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t),$ ${r}^{′}(4)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(4)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\sqrt{t-3}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{\sqrt{t-3}},1⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(4) & =⟨2,1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(4)‖ & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}=\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{″}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=4:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{\sqrt{t-3}}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{\sqrt{(t-3)^{3}}},0⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(4) & =⟨-1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(4)$ and ${r}^{″}(4)$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(4)\times {r}^{″}(4) & =⟨2,1,0⟩\times ⟨-1,0,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(4)\times {r}^{″}(4)‖ & =1\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore, the radius of the osculating circle at  $t=4$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(4) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(4){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(4)\times {r}^{″}(4)‖}=\frac{(\sqrt{5})^{3}}{\,1\,}=5\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
